title: Build your next FastAPI app faster

beats.say: FastAPI is a joy for building APIs quickly. But it deliberately leaves the rest of your app up to you. Environments, config, logging, a database, CLI commands, storage, queues, cache, Redis.
FastAPI Startkit wires all of that together, so you can focus on your product. Here's a fresh app. Let's see how it fits.
FastAPI Startkit is all about providers. Logging is a provider. FastAPI itself is a provider. Every feature plugs in the same way.
Each one registers its services, then boots once everything is ready. Add a provider to this list, and your app picks it up.
Logging uses channels instead of handlers.
A stack fans out to other channels. Daily files, the terminal, and Slack, but only for errors.
Then you pick one per environment with LOG CHANNEL. On my laptop, the terminal is plenty.
Need a database? artisan D B install publishes the config, and adds the provider for you.
Add the database extra, and that's the setup done.
Models and migrations come straight from the CLI.
Give posts a title and a body, then migrate.
The model describes the same fields.
And every query is async. Await Post all, serialize it, and that's an endpoint.
One route, and we're live.
Under pytest, dot env dot testing loads on its own, so tests get their own database.
RefreshDatabase migrates once, and rolls back after every test. Create a post, get the list, and check it's OK.
Run pytest, and we're green.
Need a frontend? Add the Vite and Inertia providers.
Vite runs with the FastAPI plugin, React, and Tailwind. Your pages are plain React components.
Here's the page, served by FastAPI and rendered with Inertia.
Change it, save, and it hot reloads. No refresh. And it's still FastAPI underneath.
So, build your next FastAPI app faster. One command. uvx fastapi-startkit at latest, init.
Pick your services, a database, and a frontend.
And it's ready. The docs and the GitHub repo are linked below. Happy building.
